facts.fact: The EU feasibility study states that the civil-status administration software HERA, promoted by the CNEC, was installed by the PAMEC project in 83 civil-status centres; it gives no total of centres, and its bibliography cites July 2017 reports on deployment and training in 80 centres. Dated to the study, April 2019.

The study states that no consolidated national civil register yet exists, that the civil register is fragmentary and not unified nationally, and that a future central system would have to be fed from the existing municipal civil-status databases and the remaining paper registers.

The study states that the Direction de l'état civil, with the Centre national de l'état civil, in the ministry of territorial governance holds the institutional mandate to coordinate the progressive computerisation of civil-status centres, under decree 2018-1573 of 27 August 2018; HERA is the software the CNEC promotes.

The study states that HERA was installed in the centres by PAMEC, the EU project financed under the 10th EDF, which targeted restricted numbers of centres for its costliest actions; the deployment report it cites is dated July 2017.
